title: Predicting Uber/Lyft Prices: KNN vs. Random Forest
text:
Description: Ride-sharing platforms such as Uber and Lyft use dynamic pricing that makes fare prediction a challenging problem. This study compares K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Regression and Random Forest in predicting ride-sharing prices using a dataset of 637,976 ride records from Boston, MA. Features include distance, surge multiplier, ride type, source, destination, and time-based attributes. KNN (k=9) achieved an RMSE of $1.841, MAE of $1.187, and R2 of 0.961, while Random Forest achieved an RMSE of $1.811, MAE of $1.142, and R2 of 0.962. Results show that both models effectively predict ride-sharing prices, with Random Forest outperforming KNN overall.

title: Bridge Infrastructure Analysis
text:
Description: This project evaluates bridge failure risk across Omaha’s Douglas County using 2025 Federal Highway Administration inspection data. Rather than relying on structural condition alone, the analysis introduces a two-dimensional risk framework that weighs deck/superstructure/substructure condition ratings against Average Daily Traffic (ADT) as a proxy for failure consequence. Of 390 bridges analyzed, 16 were flagged as higher-risk — averaging nearly 30 years older than the rest of the sample. Statistical analysis (Spearman correlation) revealed that traffic volume and structural condition are only weakly related, meaning high-traffic bridges aren’t necessarily receiving proportionally stronger maintenance.
